title: Titanium Plating Crane Lifting Eye
function: Heavy-duty crane lifting eye for plating line
alloyReason: Grade 2 CP-Ti (UNS R50400) is selected for Titanium Plating Crane Lifting Eye where formability and corrosion resistance are prioritized over absolute strength. With 40% elongation and excellent weldability, Grade 2 CP-Ti forms a stable TiO₂ passive film that provides immunity to pitting in chloride environments up to 260°C. Its 345 MPa yield strength with 30% elongation makes it ideal for Heavy-duty crane lifting eye for plating line requiring cold forming or bending without cracking. This rationale is driven by heavy-duty crane lifting eye for plating line and specific design requirements.
process: CNC machining CP Ti for plating rack geometry
TIG welding Ti filler for net-shape tolerance
Pickling and passivation for net-shape tolerance
Continuity test <1 mOhm for net-shape tolerance
surfaceTreatment: Platinum cladding 2.5um minimum via electrodeposition for stable catalytic surface in electrochemical cells — tailored for heavyduty crane lifting application
commonFailures: Uneven coating from current density variation - corrected by auxiliary anode 50mm from cathode — critical for heavyduty crane lifting performance

faq.q: What bath chemistries is Titanium Plating Crane Lifting Eye resistant to?
faq.a: Grade 2 CP-Ti used in Titanium Plating Crane Lifting Eye resists attack in hexavalent chromium plating baths (250 g/L CrO₃), sulfuric acid anodizing (15-20% H₂SO₄), nickel sulfamate (300 g/L Ni), and cyanide-based solutions where steel racks corrode at >5 mm/month. Service life in these environments exceeds 12 months continuous immersion for heavyduty crane lifting.

Sample evaluation (1-5 units) can be expedited to 5-7 business days. Volume pricing is available for production quantities above 100 units.

faq.q: What material certifications are provided with Titanium Plating Crane Lifting Eye?
faq.a: Each Titanium Plating Crane Lifting Eye shipment includes EN 10204 Type 3.1 mill test certificate with chemical analysis, mechanical properties, and heat identification. Dimensional inspection reports and Certificate of Conformance (CoC) are standard. First Article Inspection Reports (FAIR) per AS9102 are available on request for heavyduty crane lifting.
